counterfactual_missing_items: no evidence of infectious emboli or systemic infection
no other primary tumor or metastatic pattern
decisive_items: a 6×8 mm non-solid structure on the ventricular aspect of the anterior tricuspid leaflet with a “finger-in-glove” blind-ended protrusion
internally empty with filamentous adherent elements (“garland-like”)
a ~9 mm round, hyperechoic mass adherent to the ventricular surface of the anterior tricuspid leaflet
response.rationale: R1 uniquely matches the raw TEE description: a small, non-solid, mobile mass on the tricuspid leaflet with finger-in-glove and garland-like features, the classic echocardiographic signature of papillary fibroelastoma. R5's 'blood cultures were negative' is cited both as support and contradiction, indicating a self-conflicting, non-diagnostic rationale; endocarditis typically would show valvular destruction or positive cultures. R3 and R4 rely only on generic cardiovascular risk factors with no specific lesion correlation.

rejected.why: Only cites 'active smoker' without any connection to the tricuspid mass or relevant neuromuscular findings.
Cites negative blood cultures, which directly contradict an infectious etiology; no vegetations or destructive valvular features are described.
General atherosclerotic risk factors do not explain the distinctive echocardiographic mass; no plaque, thrombus, or vascular lesion matching the vignette.
